question: When you draw a shape, what should its border look like before you have picked a colour for it?
context: Every shape you draw arrives with a Border row already in its Effects list, and that border is painted the exact colour the fill is. On a filled shape you cannot see it: the panel says Border, 4 pt, Inside, and the picture has no line. Drag the width up and on an inside border nothing happens, on an outside border the box just gets bigger. The only way to a visible edge today is to open the Border colour well and pick something else. This is not an accident: a box's edge and its inside have always been the one shape colour, so turning the fill off leaves you a red outline box. The question is what a shape should look like the first time, before you have chosen anything.

options.label: A deeper shade of the fill
options.summary: Draw a box and it comes out red with a deeper red edge round it. The edge is visible from the moment the shape lands, so dragging Border Width thickens a line you can already see, and the shape still reads as one colour.
pros: The Border row in the panel matches the picture: it says 4 pt and there is a 4 pt line
Dragging Width does something visible on the first try, with no trip to the colour well
The shape keeps its identity: a red box is still a red box, just with an edge
cons: Every new box looks slightly different from today, so work in progress will not match a shape drawn last week
On a very dark fill there is not much room left to go darker
options.mitigation: The edge is one click from gone (the cross on the Border row), and on a dark fill the edge goes lighter instead of darker so it still reads.

options.label: A near-black edge, whatever the fill
options.summary: Draw a box and it comes out red with a near-black edge, the way an outlined shape looks in most drawing tools. The edge colour does not follow the fill, so every fresh shape has the same ink round it.
pros: Always legible, on any fill colour, light or dark
One predictable starting point rather than a colour that changes with the fill
Reads as a deliberate outline rather than a shading effect
cons: A strong second colour appears in your picture without you asking for it
On a dark canvas or a dark fill a black edge can look like a gap rather than a line
options.mitigation: The ink is a soft graphite rather than pure black, and one pick on the Border colour changes it for every shape you draw after.

options.label: No edge until you ask for one
options.summary: Draw a box and you get just the fill, with an empty Effects list. Adding a border is one press of the plus, and when it arrives it comes in a colour that stands out from the fill.
pros: Nothing in the panel is claiming to draw something you cannot see
A fresh shape is as simple as it looks, and the Effects list really is the things you added
The border you do add is visible the moment it appears
cons: This undoes the answer you gave earlier today, when you chose to have shapes keep arriving with their edge already listed
Outlined shapes become two moves instead of one
options.mitigation: The plus sits on the Effects header and the border arrives fully formed, so it is one click and no dialog.

options.label: Leave it as it is
options.summary: A fresh shape keeps arriving with an edge painted the same colour as its fill. It shows only when you turn the fill off, and turning the width up on a filled shape goes on doing nothing you can see.
pros: Turning the fill off still gives you an outline-only box in the shape's colour, which is where this behaviour came from
cons: The panel says Border 4 pt while the picture has no line, which is the app telling you something untrue
Dragging Border Width looks broken: on an outside border the box just grows
options.mitigation: None worth the name. The width control stays a dead end until you find the colour well yourself.
